title: Gas Pipeline for Proposed Oracle Data Center Delayed to 2027
source_used: OilPrice.com (own write-up of the regulatory filing, 14 Aug 2026); Bloomberg original 14 Aug 2026 identified but not readable
key_facts: Energy Transfer's subsidiary Transwestern Pipeline moved the in-service date of its Green Chile pipeline from 15 Aug 2026 to 1 Feb 2027 in a regulatory filing on Friday 14 Aug 2026.
The pipeline is meant to supply Oracle's proposed $165 billion Project Jupiter data center in Dona Ana County, New Mexico, near the US-Mexico border.
Project Jupiter could run on up to 2.5 gigawatts of gas-powered fuel cells from Bloom Energy; Green Chile is designed to deliver up to 400 million cubic feet of gas a day.
Oracle told federal regulators in May 2026 that 'time is of the essence' and that pipeline delays could jeopardize the project.
New Mexico's State Land Office has repeatedly declined to approve the pipeline route across a small section of state land.
Bloomberg first reported the delay on 14 Aug 2026; EnergyNow re-posted it dated 3 Oct 2026 with a URL path of 2026/08.
quote_evidence: Energy Transfer subsidiary Transwestern Pipeline pushed the expected in-service date for its Green Chile Project from August 15 to February 1, 2027, according to a regulatory filing Friday.
Oracle warned federal regulators in May that "time is of the essence" and said delays to Green Chile could jeopardize the broader project.
New Mexico's State Land Office has repeatedly declined to approve Energy Transfer's proposed pipeline route, which crosses a small section of state-owned land.
why_it_matters_hint: Even data centers that bring their own power still depend on pipelines and permits, and this one slipped six months.
notes: EnergyNow (403) re-dated an August 2026 Bloomberg story. Stale; later developments (Oracle force majeure notice, 24 Sep 2026) are not in this item. Candidate for QA hold-back.
